description.en: Build clean pulling, pushing, leg strength, trunk control, mobility, and resilient joints.
Develop pull-over control, high pulls, support strength, and assisted transitions.
Build controlled muscle-up transitions, tuck-lever foundations and supported handstand practice.
Repeat clean supported skills, strengthen tuck shapes and develop balanced full-body strength.
Develop longer-lever strength, controlled muscle-ups and handstand balance while maintaining full-body fundamentals and flexibility.
Consolidate strong basics and explore handstand, flag, lever and planche variations at your current ability. Use regressions freely; there is no mastery deadline.

Train brief full front and back levers, the full human flag, freestanding handstand push-up negatives and one-arm pull-up groundwork in small daily doses, with the straddle shapes and assisted rungs always in the same class to step back to.

authentic_description.en: Start with the warm-up, practise the strength sequence at a controllable difficulty, then finish with the cooldown.

catalog_notice.en: Replacement and extension sessions are newly authored for StreetGym. The app uses a balanced seven-level sequence of 100 assigned workouts per level.

progression_readiness.en: Advance a movement only after you can complete its current variation with controlled range and reserve effort on at least two separate sessions. Change only one variable: repetitions, hold time, assistance or lever length. A new workout number is not a skill-readiness test; keep using an easier variation as long as needed. Later planche, straddle and full-lever shapes are practice ceilings, not requirements: use the listed regression for as long as needed. The levels build challenge through harder variations and controlled workload, with easier consolidation days between demanding sessions. Keep the current variation until it is repeatable; a shorter lever or more assistance can still be challenging training.

training_recovery.en: Follow the assigned morning class, including its easy recovery sessions. Daily practice does not mean daily hard effort. If soreness or fatigue makes the warm-up unusually heavy, make today an easy walk and mobility morning, then return to the assigned strength session when recovered.

authentic_scaling.en: The morning version limits strength plus skill practice to 14 sets in Foundations, 16 in Bar Strength and 18 in Skill Transition, with at most 3 sets per exercise, 12 repetitions or 30 seconds per hold. Former max sets are capped at 8 quality repetitions. These are ceilings: stop sooner with 2-3 repetitions in reserve and keep effort at RPE 6 in Foundations and 7 in later levels, or below. Use foot-assisted hangs and pulls, higher rows, incline push-ups, assisted dips or bent-knee raises when needed. Steps the program has not prepared yet (behind-the-neck pulls, head bangers, hanging L-sits, early muscle-ups and unassisted inversions) already appear as library movements, each with its easier option. Inversions and turnovers require controlled entries, exits and suitable assistance. Recovery mornings are already assigned.

app_slot_order.purpose: Source slot shown at each app position, per level; levels not listed keep slot order. Level 2 runs its 40 reconstructed bridge classes (source slots 31-70) before the 30 original-source workouts (slots 1-30), so the source block arrives after pull-ups, chest-to-bar, knee raises and tuck L-sits are trained. Reconstructed records are numbered by app position; source content and legacy ids follow their slot.
